Client: Aularis Strategies

Create one connected business process for each of the eight explicitly named phases below. These are eight phases, not five summary flows. They must be ordered 1 through 8 and connected by normal completion handoffs. Preserve loops, gates, renewable and film variants, external parties, inputs, outputs, controls, and open validation gaps.

The source map has seven role lanes including Solution Architecture & Technical. Remove Solution Architecture & Technical as a business lane. Do not remove its work. Reassign education materials, technical Q&A, compliance design/code monitoring, and the advisor/investor technical desk to Compliance & Client Experience, with the accountable owner marked TBD and Nate retained only as a supporting technical subject-matter expert where useful.

Use these six remaining business lanes throughout the portfolio:
1. Referring Advisor & Client
2. Business Development & Capital — Billy, Chief Revenue Officer; VFO Hub supports advisor compensation
3. Engagement, Closing & Systems — Steph owns project flow; Malcolm owns systems and automation
4. Project Diligence & Information — Brian owns renewable/project execution; Michelle owns film projects
5. Compliance & Client Experience — accountable owner currently TBD
6. Counsel, Escrow & Counterparties — panel counsel, escrow agent, developer or producer, and return preparer

Phase 01 — Advisor Education & Sales
- Develop capital partnerships. Input: target advisor/RIA profile and program economics. Output: advisor pipeline and referring-firm relationships. Billy owns capital partnerships.
- Onboard advisor as a VFO Hub member firm. Input: VFO Hub consulting agreement. Output: member-firm status and compensation eligibility. Aularis does not pay client advisors directly.
- Produce education and program materials. Inputs: code positions and deal assumptions. Outputs: program guide, participation-hours guide, illustration model, and versioned Terms and Conditions. Compliance & Client Experience is the business lane; Nate may support as technical SME.
- Conduct advisor education session. Inputs: program guide and client floors. Output: shortlist of candidate clients.
- Advisor presents program to client. Output: client interest and rough capacity. Aularis supports but does not replace the client's advisor.
- Source and pipeline projects begins in parallel. Brian owns renewable developer pipeline; Michelle owns completed-but-unreleased film sourcing. Output: project pipeline with timing and size.
- Normal exit artifact: qualified advisor/client opportunity plus current program and project materials.

Phase 02 — Expression of Interest & Sizing
- Build Aularis illustration. Inputs: client capacity and illustration model. Outputs: investment size, purchase deposit, consulting fee, projected benefits, and schedule. Source assumptions to validate: purchase deposit about 40 percent of transaction value and fee equal to 20 percent of projected depreciation.
- Technical Q&A on the illustration. Reassign to Compliance & Client Experience; Nate is supporting SME. Output: written answers/positions summary.
- Advisor confirms fit with the client's other planning. Output: advisor sign-off and sizing decision.
- Decision gateway: EOI addendum submitted — proceed? No returns to sizing or closes the opportunity. Yes fixes the fee assumptions, opens the transaction, hands off to Phase 03, and also starts participation onboarding.
- Film floors are assumptions requiring validation: minimum $250,000 deposit and at least $500,000 annual income. Confirm whether renewable uses the same floors.
- Exit artifact: approved non-binding EOI and locked assumption set.

Phase 03 — Intake
- Engagement Agreement and version-locked T&Cs signed. Steph owns project flow; Malcolm supports signature automation. Output: executed engagement.
- Client intake package. Inputs: client/advisor data. Outputs: KYC/identity, investing entity and W-9, tax profile for K-1 reporting, eligibility confirmation, and advisor member-firm confirmation.
- Client engages panel counsel using the firm's own engagement letter. Validate 0.725 percent basic versus 1.45 percent tax-plus-transaction scope and $5,000/$10,000 minimums.
- Match client to project and assemble diligence package. Owners: Brian for renewable and Michelle for film. Outputs: diligence package and closing calendar.
- Participation onboarding — hours start now. Lane: Compliance & Client Experience, owner TBD. Inputs: participation guide and logging tool. Outputs: client orientation and first logged hours. Pre-admission-hour position requires legal/tax validation.
- Exit artifacts: intake-complete client file, counsel engagement, matched project/diligence package, and active participation log.

Phase 04 — Escrow Coordination
- Issue escrow instructions. Owner: Steph. Inputs: executed engagement and EOI amounts. Outputs: services/fee escrow with counsel earmark and a separate purchase-deposit/capital bucket.
- Client wires deposits. Advisor coordinates; client funds. Aularis confirms receipt but does not hold client money outside escrow.
- Escrow agent receives and holds funds. Output: receipt confirmation for both buckets.
- Decision gateway: confirm funds and reconcile to EOI. Failure returns for discrepancy resolution. Success marks the transaction funded and releases Phase 05.
- Versioned control: through 2026 the client funds the counsel earmark; proposed 2027 process has Aularis paying counsel directly.
- Exit artifact: funded/reconciled status plus escrow evidence.

Phase 05 — Closing
- Final diligence and closing checklist. Owners: Brian or Michelle. Inputs: diligence package and funded status. Output: asset-level checklist complete.
- Panel counsel reviews for client. Output: counsel sign-off. Counsel represents the client, not Aularis.
- Execute closing and admit Member/Managers. Owner: Steph. Inputs: checklist, counsel sign-off, funded status. Outputs: operating agreement, admission, and services covenant up to 110 hours.
- Settlement statement and disbursement. Owners: Steph and escrow agent. Outputs: all developer/promoter/facilitator disclosures, counsel payment, consulting-fee release, and purchase deposit released to project.
- Compensation flows. Billy owns. Validate 2026 assumptions: VFO Hub receives 67.5 percent of fee collected, transaction attorney receives 75 basis points of transaction value, and developer financing consulting fee is separate.
- Exit artifacts: executed closing set, admission record, settlement statement, compensation ledger, and project funding.

Phase 06 — 100+ Hour Compliance
- Client performs and logs services such as meetings, diligence trips, site visits, and production visits. Output: contemporaneous entries with specific descriptions.
- Run activity program and hour tracking. Lane: Compliance & Client Experience, owner TBD. Output: scheduled activities and monthly status by member.
- Description review and QC. AI may check specificity, business connection, and travel-rule consistency; a human reviews exceptions. Output: clean log and deficiency notices.
- Keep other active participants below threshold. Inputs: service contracts and counterparty reports. Output: evidence that non-member active participants remain below member hours.
- Compliance design and code monitoring. Reassign to Compliance & Client Experience; Nate supports as technical SME. Outputs: updated positions, guides, and T&C versions.
- Decision gateway: year-end participation certification. If below 100 hours, start remediation before year-end. If met, produce certification and CPA support package.
- Exit artifacts: quality-controlled log, threshold evidence, and participation certification.

Phase 07 — Technical Support
- Advisor and investor technical desk. Lane: Compliance & Client Experience, owner TBD; Nate supports as technical SME. Inputs: advisor/CPA/investor questions. Outputs: written answers, position summaries, and FAQs. Information only; no advice on an individual return.
- Partnership return and K-1 preparation. External return preparer, coordinated by Aularis. Inputs: entity books, member tax profiles, and participation certifications. Outputs: partnership return, K-1s, and supporting information. Validate the approximate $5,000-per-entity assumption.
- Advisor/CPA integrates K-1 into client return. Owners: client's professionals. Output: client return prepared by those professionals. Aularis supplies information but not return advice.
- Advisor relations and program updates. Billy and VFO Hub communicate changes and reconcile compensation.
- Exit artifacts: K-1 package, technical support record, and advisor update.

Phase 08 — Ongoing Maintenance
- Inclusive program gateway: renewable, film, or both applicable oversight paths.
- Renewable path: placed-in-service confirmation, O&M oversight, annual credit compliance, and recapture-risk monitoring. Owner: Brian.
- Film path: producer, distribution, and CAMA oversight; performance analysis; credentialing; distribution tracking; and about 10 percent back-end participation monitoring. Owner: Michelle. Validate later-year management-fee and year-five consolidation assumptions.
- Annual entity administration. Owners: Malcolm and Steph. Outputs: return cycle, K-1 coordination, member communications, and applicable fee accrual.
- Members continue engagement at the maintenance level. Owners: client and advisor.
- Renewal to next transaction. Billy owns. Success loops back to Phase 01 through the advisor channel.
- Exit artifacts: annual administration file, program oversight record, member communications, and renewed/referral opportunity.

Required cross-process behavior:
- Connect Phase 01 through Phase 08 in order with explicit entry and exit criteria and transferred artifacts.
- Model the Phase 02 approved-EOI handoff to both Phase 03 intake and the Phase 03 participation-onboarding work.
- Model Phase 04 funding failure as rework and success as the Phase 05 release gate.
- Model renewable and film variants without duplicating shared work.
- Model Phase 08 renewal as a loop back to Phase 01.
- Use consistent activity names across phases so AIReady Foundry can reuse components.
- Do not invent source code paths, APIs, MCP tools, URLs, systems, or credentials. Leave those arrays empty when not supplied and mark technical discovery as required.
- Every process needs a specific start and end event, internal connections, owners, controls, inputs, outputs, lane names, predecessor/successor references, and measurable exit criteria.

Open validation gaps:
- Accountable owner for Compliance & Client Experience
- Owner of the CPA relationship, return-preparation coordination, and K-1 support
- Renewable eligibility floors
- Legal/tax basis for pre-admission hours and the 100/110-hour operating rule
- Counsel payment mechanics for 2027
- In-house versus panel-counsel scope
- Every fee, percentage, minimum, deposit ratio, facilitator payment, management fee, retention rule, evidence requirement, and access-control requirement

Return all eight connected process drafts for review. Do not save or mark them validated.
